_comment: In-the-wild CUDA artifacts: the distribution forms real users actually run (PyPI wheels, conda packages, container images, and adversarially stripped/renamed copies). Each entry is content-pinned (sha256 for downloads, image digest for containers) so the eval is reproducible. 'expect' records known ground truth where the package declares it; entries with no version are scored detection-only. Downloads land under the gitignored corpus/distribution dir; nothing large is committed.

artifacts.note: nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12: official NVIDIA PyPI wheel; declares version in package metadata. Syft's home turf.
nvidia-cudnn-cu12 9.0.0.312: bundles libcudnn*.so under nvidia/cudnn/lib.
nvidia-nccl-cu12 2.27.7: bundles libnccl.so under nvidia/nccl/lib.

cupy-cuda12x 14.2.0: a THIRD-PARTY wheel that vendors CUDA runtime libraries. The package version (14.2.0) is CuPy's, not CUDA's, and the bundled libs carry no PyPI metadata of their own: the adversarial 'vendored, renamed, no metadata' case. Detection-only: we record whether each tool names ANY CUDA component and whether cudabom pins the bundled CUDA versions.
nvidia channel libcublas 13.4.1.3 (.conda = zip of zstd-compressed tars). Ships the REAL libcublas.so under targets/x86_64-linux/lib (not just the lib/ symlink shims some conda metapackages use).

nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04, pinned by image digest. The container-scanning home turf for Trivy/Syft. cudabom scans the exported filesystem for CUDA libraries; Trivy/Syft scan the image natively.

Generated locally from an already-present corpus library: a COPY that is stripped (symbols/soname removed) and renamed to an innocuous name (e.g. libplugin.so). This defeats name/soname heuristics; only a content hash or build-id survives. Source is resolved from the redist corpus at run time, so nothing is downloaded or committed.

Windows deployment form: a cudart64_12.dll copied and renamed to an innocuous name (plugin.dll). Exercises the PE/DLL identification path on a renamed binary. Source is the Windows redist already in the corpus.

Pure static deployment: the self-contained static runtime libcudart_static.a, which a statically linked app compiles in (no .so at all). cudabom identifies static CUDA by hashing the archive's member objects. The harness links an executable when a matching toolchain exists, else scans the .a directly (the same member-hash path).

Adversarial: a CUDA library UPX-compressed. The on-disk bytes change, so a file-hash match is defeated; the finding is whether ANY signal survives (likely a MISS, recorded honestly). Needs upx on PATH; without it the copy is scanned unpacked.

Adversarial: a CUDA library concatenated inside a larger blob at a non-zero offset (as a vendored payload embedded in another file would appear). Tests whether the library is identified when it is not the whole file. Resolved by embedded-ELF offset scanning: the library's build-id/symbols identify it at its byte offset even though the whole-file hash matches nothing.
Version spread (old): nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu11 11.8.89, the CUDA 11.x line. Confirms identification across major generations, not just current 12.x/13.x.
Non-x86 platform: nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12 12.4.127 built for aarch64 (ARM / Grace, Jetson-adjacent). Confirms the identification path is not x86-only.

Fat ML container: pytorch/pytorch 2.5.1-cuda12.4-cudnn9-runtime, pinned by digest. CUDA arrives via pip wheels vendored into the image's site-packages (nvidia/*), a harder container case than the clean nvidia/cuda base. Trivy/Syft scan the image natively; cudabom scans the exported filesystem.
Fat ML container: tensorflow/tensorflow 2.17.0-gpu, pinned by digest. TensorFlow bundles its own CUDA libraries; another real-world fat-image case.
